question.text:
Consider the system
\[ \begin{cases} -x_1+2x_3=2 \\ x_2-3x_3=1 \\ 2x_1 -4x_3 = -4. \end{cases} \] Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
question.explanation:
The augmented matrix for the system is

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} -1 & 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & -4 & -4 \end{array} \right]. \]

Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

\[\begin{align*} M&\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} -1 & 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & -4 & -4 \end{array}\right] & R_1 &:=-R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & -4 & -4 \end{array}\right]& R_3 &:= R_3 +(-2)R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right]. \end{align*}\]

question.text: Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by \[ M= \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right]. \] Find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
question.explanation:
Notice that the matrix $M$ is already in row echelon form. The system corresponding to $M$ is

\[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} x - 2y + 3z = -2 \\ 0x + y - 6z = 2 \\ 0x + 0y + 0z = 0. \end{array} \right. \]

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final equation $0x+0y+0z = 0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of just two equations:

\[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} x - 2y + 3z = -2 \\ y - 6z = 2 \end{array} \right. \]

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ To do this, we apply the back substitution.

From the second equation, we get

\[ y - 6z = 2 \quad\Rightarrow\quad y = 6z + 2 \]

and substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

\[ x - 2(6z + 2) + 3z = -2 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x = 9z +2. \]

Therefore, the general solution is

\[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} x= 9z+2 \\ y= 6z + 2 \\ z= z, \end{array} \right. \]

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as \[ \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 9z+2 \\ 6z+2 \\ z \end{bmatrix}, \qquad z \in (-\infty,\infty). \]

question.text: Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by \[ M= \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 0 & -1 &1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ \end{array}\right]. \] Find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
question.explanation:
Notice that the matrix $M$ is already in row echelon form. The system corresponding to $M$ is

\[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} x + 0y - z = 1 \\ 0x + y + 3z = 2 \\ 0x + 0y + 0z = 0. \end{array} \right. \]

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final equation $0x+0y+0z = 0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of just two equations:

\[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} x - z = 1 \\ y + 3z = 2 \end{array} \right. \]

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ To do this, we apply the back substitution.

From the second equation, we get

\[ y + 3z = 2 \quad\Rightarrow\quad y = 2 - 3z \]

and from the first equation, we obtain

\[ x - z = 1 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x = 1 + z. \]

Therefore, the general solution is

\[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} x=1 +z \\ y=2 - 3z \\ z= z, \end{array} \right. \]

where $z$ (the free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as \begin{align*} \begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}1+z \\ 2 - 3z \\ z \end{bmatrix}, \qquad z \in (-\infty,\infty). \end{align*}

question.text:
Consider the system
\[ \begin{cases} -2x_1+4x_3=4 \\ x_2-5x_3=3 \\ 3x_1 -6x_3 = -6. \end{cases} \] Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
question.explanation:
The augmented matrix for this system is \[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} -2 & 0 & 4 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & 3 \\ 3 & 0 & -6 & -6 \end{array} \right]. \]

Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

\[\begin{align*} M&\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} -2 & 0 & 4 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & 3 \\ 3 & 0 & -6 & -6 \end{array}\right] & R_1 &:=-\dfrac{1}{2}R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & 3 \\ 3 & 0 & -6 & -6 \end{array}\right]& R_3 &:= R_3 +(-3)R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right]. \end{align*}\]

question.text:
Consider the system
\[ \begin{cases} -2x_1 + 6x_2 + 2x_3 = -8 \\ x_1 - 2x_2 + x_3 = 2 \\ -3x_1 + 9x_2 + 3x_3 = -12. \end{cases} \] Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
question.explanation:
The augmented matrix for the system is

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{ccc|c} -2 & 6 & 2 & -8 \\ 1 & -2 & 1 & 2 \\ -3 & 9 & 3 & -12 \end{array} \right]. \]

Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

\[\begin{align*} M&\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} -2 & 6 & 2 & -8 \\ 1 & -2 & 1 & 2 \\ -3 & 9 & 3 & -12 \end{array}\right] & R_1 &:= -\dfrac 1 2R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -3 & -1 & 4 \\ 1 & -2 & 1 & 2 \\ -3 & 9 & 3 & -12 \end{array}\right]& R_2 &:= R_2 +(-1)R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -3 & -1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -2 \\ -3 & 9 & 3 & -12 \end{array}\right]& R_3 &:= R_3 + 3R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -3 & -1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right]. \end{align*}\]

question.text: Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by \[ M= \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -3 & -5 & -6 \\ 4 & -12 & -20 & -24 \\ -\dfrac{1}{2} & \dfrac{3}{2} & \dfrac{5}{2} & 3 \\ \end{array}\right]. \] Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
question.explanation:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have \[\begin{align*} M&\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -3 & -5 & -6 \\ 4 & -12 & -20 & -24 \\ -\dfrac{1}{2} & \dfrac{3}{2} & \dfrac{5}{2} & 3 \\ \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2 - 4R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -3 & -5 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -\dfrac{1}{2} & \dfrac{3}{2} & \dfrac{5}{2} & 3 \\ \end{array}\right]& R_3 &:= R_3 + \dfrac{1}{2}R_1 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -3 & -5 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ \end{array}\right].\\ \end{align*}\]

The corresponding system is now \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} x - 3y - 5z = -6 \\ 0x + 0y + 0z = 0 \\ 0x + 0y + 0z = 0. \end{array} \right. \]

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final two equations $0x+0y+0z = 0,$ we can remove these equations from the system. So, our system now consists of just a single equation: \[ x - 3y - 5z = -6 \]

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$, and we have two free variables $y$ and $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y,z.$ Doing this, we get

\[ x = -6 + 3y + 5z. \]

Therefore, the general solution is \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} x=-6 + 3y + 5z \\ y=y \\ z=z \end{array} \right. \]

where $y,z$ (the free variables) are arbitrary numbers.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

\begin{align*} \begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -6 + 3y + 5z \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix}, \qquad y,z \in (-\infty,\infty). \end{align*}

question.text: Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by \[ M= \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} -1 & 5 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right]. \] Find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
question.explanation:
The system corresponding to $M$ is \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} -x + 5y + 0z = 3 \\ 0x + 0y + 0z = 0 \\ 0x + 0y + 0z = 0. \end{array} \right. \]

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final two equations $0x+0y+0z = 0,$ we can remove these equations from the system. So, our system now consists of just a single equation:

\[ -x + 5y = 3 \]

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$, and we have two free variables $y$ and $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y,z.$ Doing this, we get

\[ x = 5y-3. \]

Therefore, the general solution is

\[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} x=5y-3 \\ y=y \\ z=z, \end{array} \right. \]

where $y$, $z$ (free variables) are arbitrary numbers.

In vector form, the solution can be written as \begin{align*} \begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 5y-3 \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} + y \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} + z \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad y,z \in (-\infty,\infty). \end{align*}

question.text: Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by \[ M= \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -1 & 4 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right]. \] Find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
question.explanation:
The system corresponding to $M$ is \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} x - y + 4z = -1 \\ 0x + 0y + 0z = 0 \\ 0x + 0y + 0z = 0. \end{array} \right. \]

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final two equations $0x+0y+0z = 0,$ we can remove these equations from the system. So, our system now consists of just a single equation:

\[ x - y + 4z = -1 \]

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$, and we have two free variables $y$ and $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y,z.$ Doing this, we get

\[ x = -1+y-4z. \]

Therefore, the general solution is

\[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} x=-1+y-4z \\ y=y \\ z=z, \end{array} \right. \]

where $y$, $z$ (free variables) are arbitrary numbers.

In vector form, the solution can be written as \begin{align*} \begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -1+y-4z \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} + y \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix} + z \begin{bmatrix} -4 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}, \qquad y,z \in (-\infty,\infty). \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Identifying a Singular 3x3 System of Equations That Has No Solution

question.text: Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by \[ M= \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 3 & -5 & 6 \\ 3 & 10 & -12 & 14 \\ 2 & 3 & -19 & 15 \\ \end{array}\right]. \] Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
question.explanation:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

\[ \begin{align*} M&\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 3 & -5 & 6 \\ 3 & 10 & -12 & 14 \\ 2 & 3 & -19 & 15 \\ \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2-3R_1\\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 3 & -5 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -4 \\ 2 & 3 & -19 & 15 \\ \end{array}\right]& R_3 &:= R_3 -2R_1\\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 3 & -5 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -4 \\ 0& -3 & -9 & 3 \\ \end{array}\right]&R_3 &:= R_3+3R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & 3 & -5 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -4 \\ 0& 0 & 0 & -9 \\ \end{array}\right].\\ \end{align*} \]

The corresponding system is now

\[ \begin{cases} x + 3y - 5z = 6 \\ 0x + y + 3z = -4 \\ 0x + 0y + 0z = -9 \end{cases} \]

Since there are no such numbers $x,y,z$ that form a solution of the final equation $0x+0y+0z = -9,$ we can conclude that our system has no solution.

question.text: Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by \[ M= \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & -6 &12 \\ 2 & 4 & 12 & -16 \\ 1 & -4 & -12 & 21 \\ \end{array}\right]. \] Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.

Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

\[ \begin{align*} M&\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & -6 &12 \\ 2 & 4 & 12 & -16 \\ 1 & -4 & -12 & 21 \\ \end{array}\right] & R_2 &:= R_2-2R_1\\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & -6 &12 \\ 0 & 8 & 24 & -40 \\ 1 & -4 & -12 & 21 \\ \end{array}\right]& R_3 &:= R_3 -R_1\\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & -6 &12 \\ 0 & 8 & 24 & -40 \\ 0& -2 & -6 & 9 \\ \end{array}\right]&R_2 &:= \dfrac 1 8 R_2\\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & -6 &12 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -5 \\ 0& -2 & -6 & 9 \\ \end{array}\right]&R_3&:= R_3+2R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c} 1 & -2 & -6 &12 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -5 \\ 0& 0 & 0 & -1 \end{array}\right].\\ \end{align*} \]

The corresponding system is now

\[ \begin{cases} x - 2y - 6z = 12 \\ 0x + y + 3z = -5 \\ 0x + 0y + 0z = -1 \end{cases} \]

Since there are no such numbers $x,y,z$ that form a solution of the final equation $0x+0y+0z = -1,$ we can conclude that our system has no solution.
